items.t: Chinese Tea Traditions in Modern Times
items.s: Ancient Chinese tea ceremonies are evolving with contemporary lifestyles, blending millennia-old traditions with modern innovations to create new cultural experiences.

items.t: China's Tea Traditions in Modern Times
items.s: Discover how ancient Chinese tea culture blends with contemporary lifestyles, creating new experiences for tea enthusiasts worldwide.

items.t: China's Coffee Capital Brews a Global Financial Stir
items.s: Shanghai has quietly become the world's most crowded coffee market, turning a daily caffeine habit into a fierce commercial arena. This beverage boom is now drawing major consumer-finance attention as global funds pour capital into domestic chains.

items.t: China's Running Revolution: Marathon Culture Blooms
items.s: Once a nation of cyclists, China has embraced running marathons with unprecedented enthusiasm, creating one of the world's largest and most vibrant running communities.

items.t: China's High-Speed Rail Network Connects Ancient and Modern
items.s: China's expanding high-speed rail network transforms travel across the world's most populous nation, connecting historic sites with modern cities at unprecedented speeds.

items.t: Marathon Madness: How Running Became China's Weekend Ritual
items.s: From mega-city marathons with lottery entry to trail races in the mountains, tens of millions of Chinese runners have turned weekend racing into a national pastime.

items.t: A Nation of Tea Drinkers Falls for Coffee
items.s: China now runs one of the world's largest coffee markets. From Shanghai's specialty roasters to app-driven chains, coffee has quietly become part of everyday urban life.

items.t: Seeing China at 350 km/h: A Practical High-Speed Rail Guide
items.s: With over 45,000 kilometers of high-speed lines linking megacities and ancient towns, China's bullet-train network is the fastest way for visitors to see the country. Here is how to use it.
